content.text:
This References and Compliance Library consolidates all authoritative sources that underpin the policies, procedures, and practices outlined in this Principal's Handbook. The library serves multiple critical functions:

**For Regulatory Compliance:** Provides direct access to Indonesian national education regulations, enabling schools to verify compliance with Ministry of Education requirements, Yayasan obligations, and national curriculum mandates.

**For Accreditation Readiness:** Links to CIS and WASC standards documentation, supporting self-study preparation and evidence compilation for accreditation cycles.

**For Cambridge Centre Operations:** References Cambridge International's official handbooks, guides, and policy documents essential for maintaining Centre status and examination integrity.

**For Professional Practice:** Curates best-practice resources for English as an Additional Language (EAL), Special Educational Needs (SEN), and Multi-Tiered System of Supports (MTSS) implementation.

**For Evidence Management:** The Reference Index (Appendix 20.1) tracks version numbers, update dates, and responsible officers to ensure schools maintain current documentation.

content.title: 20.4.1 CIS Framework Documentation
Note on this table
content.text:
A note on the word "retired": an earlier revision of this manual said the CIS lettered domains had been retired in favour of eighteen standards across three dimensions. That was wrong and has been withdrawn - see the correction note in Section 18.2.

The CIS International Accreditation Evaluation Framework [Revised] is organised in 8 domains carrying 45 standards, of which 24 are core, plus a further domain of 8 standards (5 core) for schools with boarding or homestay - lettered A to I. CIS Instructions for Submission, updated August 2024, addresses schools hosting visits in 2025 under that framework, so it is live.

What IS changing is that CIS issued a successor framework built on Three Dimensions and Cornerstones (Process Overview v1.0, October 2024) to early-adopter schools ahead of a public launch.

So a "CIS Domain X" reference in this manual is correct in form; check the domain NAME against the official titles in Section 18.2, and confirm with CIS which framework your own visit will use.

A duplicate copy of this note, and a second table that restated the withdrawn 18-standard scheme as if it were current, were removed from this section on 2026-08-20.

content.title: Note on this table
content.text:
Two corrections to the source image.

First, EASE was described as a single "Evaluation of Achievement Standardized Exam"; under the current model EASE (Eduversal Analytical & Skills Evaluation) is an umbrella brand with three programs - EASE Growth, EASE Assessment (also called Common Assessment) and EASE Academic.

Second, the image listed the EduNav platform as the live quality-management dashboard and evidence repository. That is correct and the question raised in an earlier revision — whether EduNav might be a legacy product — is settled: EduNav is Eduversal's current school information system, developed by PT. Global Zerone Digital for Eduversal and defined at clause 4.3.2, and it is listed among the QMS products at clause 1.3 (DTP, Appraisal, EduOS, EduNav, EASE).

The EduNav storage instructions in Sections 19 and 20 therefore point at the right system. Where a storage instruction reads "Google Drive, EduNav, or similar", keep that hedged form — it is what allows an instruction to survive a future change of platform.

content.title: Eduversal quality management system components
rows: Umbrella assessment brand (Eduversal Analytical & Skills Evaluation) covering three programs: EASE Growth (student reasoning and literacy benchmark, curriculum-independent), EASE Assessment (centralized chapter-end and semester-end subject tests; also called Common Assessment), and EASE Academic (teacher subject and pedagogical knowledge; formative, for professional development only).

content.title: Note on this index
content.text: Rebuilt by Eduversal on 2026-08-17. The original index was lost in conversion. This version is derived from the corrected corpus rather than from the lost original, so it carries the corrections made in the 2026-08-17 audit: CIS domains are lettered A-I with their official titles (the numbered scheme is retired), ACS WASC runs Categories A-D only, breach notification is UU No. 27/2022 Pasal 46(1), safeguarding answers to Permendikdasmen No. 6/2026 (BSAN), educator standards to Permendikdasmen No. 21/2025, and yayasan governance to UU No. 16/2001 jo. UU No. 28/2004. This index is a NAVIGATION AID, not an authority. Each section states its own references in full, with article and page citations; where this index and a section differ, the section governs. Re-check the index whenever a section's regulatory basis changes.
